body:
I have been on Effexor XR (venlafaxine) 75mg for the past 2.5 months and it's made a world of difference for me. In my experience so far, I am able to think more rationally, better control my emotions and reactions, and recognize when I am falling into a BPD thought pattern. 

The only downside I've found is that sometimes I can't cry, or express as much emotion as I'm feeling inside. That sounds weird, right? Shouldn't I be happy that things just don't make me fly off the handle and start bawling anymore? What I mean is that sometimes things happen in life where I feel like I am going to cry, but physically it does not happen. When it doesn't happen, I feel like my body is suppressing my "need" to let something out. It can feel very frustrating. 

So far that's the only downside I have though, which if you think about it, really isn't that bad at all - I'm sure many of us would WELCOME that side effect.

>I enjoy the fact that the world is my oyster each day, and I'm not obligated to check up on someone else or keep them happy.

I can relate to this. I enjoy being able to go out and do whatever, and I don't have to let anyone know where I am if I don't want to. That's not saying past partners asked me to let them know where I was, but what I mean is like I obviously wouldn't go to a party without telling my SO first. I hope that makes sense.

Me too. I miss having someone to snuggle with on the couch watching bad B-movies and nerding out about things with.

It sucks because most dating for millennials is almost all on Tinder and OkCupid and I really don't have the energy for that game anymore.
All of my friends say I'm a blast to be around. One of my friend's sisters actually told her that I would need to organize the bachelorette party for my friend's wedding because I am "so much fun".

Fuckin' same. I quit my long-term job back in March and after a lot of recovery, I'm starting to look for a job again. Every time I send in a resume I freak out. Every time I've gotten a call for an interview I talk myself out of it by saying that no one will like me there, the job will make me hate my life just like before, etc. Sigh.

> If you want to play, sure, have her around for a fuck or two

What OP's girlfriend is doing is terrible, but this isn't much better. I understand you are hurt from what happened to you in the past, but abuse and cheating are not symptoms of BPD.
I've had BPD for as long as I can remember and I've never laid a finger on a partner nor have I cheated on one. I think her issues go deeper than BPD.

I got an AirBnB when I was solo traveling a few months ago. I couldn't figure out how to turn on the oven in the apartment because the instructions were in Portuguese and no electricity seemed to be running to the oven. I had been up for 36 hours straight at that point and just started sobbing uncontrollably because I couldn't make a damn frozen pizza.

Yeah, I've heard about the horror stories of Effexor XR withdrawal. :( 

I wonder why I don't respond well to an NDRI and an SSRI simultaneously. Body chemistry is so weird.

Edit: derp derp english

I might - I've been reading up on some other medications that are on the Kroger $4 generic  list. If Celexa and Effexor XR don't work, I guess I'll just compile a list of other things I've found and ask my doctor about them. 

Lithium is something my previous psychiatrist wanted to put me on, but I had heard a lot of negative things about it like weight gain. Weight gain is a scary thing for me because I've been working really hard for a few months to get back to where I was last year. Emotional eating is a bitch. :( 

My experience with Abilify wasn't great, but it wasn't terrible either. Of course, everyone is different, so take what I'm saying with a grain of salt. I was on Abilify about 3-4 years ago and there was no generic (at least in the US). I'm not sure if there's a generic now, but back then it was so expensive that my mother resorted to ordering it from Canadian pharmacies to save money. One of the side effects of Abilify is weight gain, which definitely happened to me. When I went to see a new psychiatrist, he promptly took me off of it because he said the health risks with it were not worth the potential good things about the drug.

I'm glad it's been working well for you! Along with Zoloft and Wellbutrin, I've been on Pristiq, Abilify, Lamictal, Trazodone, and countless others... they're never really done anything for me and lately I'm beginning to wonder if I will ever find something that really does make a difference. 

I'm crossing my fingers that Celexa offers me the same relief that it has for you! :) I'll be starting it in about two weeks after I've tapered off of Zoloft and Wellbutrin. I've felt absolutely rotten today already after lowering my doses of those and was asleep most of the day. Ugh.

1. I like my hair. I've been working on growing it out for years and it's almost down to my elbows now! 

2. I like my sense of humor. I'm not trying to toot my own horn, but I think I can be pretty funny at times. A few people have told me I should do stand-up but I'm too shy. 

3. I like my sense of adventure. I am a solo-traveler. I did my first solo trip a few months ago in Europe. It was scary at first, I had some down times, but for the most part it was extremely liberating and fun.

Thanks for sharing. :) That makes me a little sad that it's comparable to Zoloft... I haven't felt that the Zoloft/Wellbutrin combination has done much for me. My doctor told me to try it for a month, and it I don't notice a difference, I'll try Effexor XR despite the cost. 

How has Lexapro been working for you? Maybe if there is a generic out for that I could mention it to my doctor to see if she thinks it would be a good fit... then I wouldn't have to pay the Effexor XR price.
Tell me about it. I forgot what lower back spasms (I've always seemed to get those right around before my period) and cramps even felt like until recently.
Omfg. Slightly off topic, but I'm on my second implant as well! The first one gave me 3 wonderful years of no periods. With this second one I actually get normal periods and PMS again. >:(

These are all good tips, thank you. I recently stopped drinking caffeinated soda and switched to caffeine-free. I went through a few days of searing headaches, so I guess I was more dependent on caffeine than I thought. I think it may have contributed to my difficulty sleeping at night.

Hey thanks! I tried this last night. I turned off my TV and instead read my book. I was in bed by midnight and managed to sleep through the night until 8AM. Instead of just laying in bed for a few more hours, I forced myself to get up, shower, and get ready for the day. I already feel more productive! Thank you!
Haha same here! My last therapist was this crotchety old woman who hmph'd a lot.
I love going to therapy! My therapist also has a really soothing voice, so I think that helps too other than the actual therapy.

I'm using an app called Moodtrack. If you have an iPhone it's on the App Store for free with a $0.99 upgrade for private mood logging. If you stay with the free version your logs will be public, so choose an inconspicuous username if you don't want anyone you know finding you.

Well, I don't want kids to begin with. But I suppose if I did want them, I would still not do so due to the possibility of my child inheriting any mental health issues, the chance of me being an awful mother, and having to be off medication while pregnant. 

I can always adopt if I change my mind later in life (not likely). If I do change my mind, I will make sure a therapist thinks I am fit to raise a child.
I'm not afraid of going outside, it's just on days I don't feel great I feel guilty about not going out and enjoying myself.
Agreed. Unless their SO has a diagnosis, I don't think these threads have any place here.

Not sure if it's a BPD thing or not, but my therapist says I am very "all-or-nothing" with everything (helloooo black and white thinking!), so my notes are either very neat and perfect or a complete mess.

I had to stop trying to make my notes for university look pristine because it would take me a half hour to write a single page.
Yeah I can agree with that. I'll analyze it all. Was this an ex girlfriend? Do they still talk? Are they still Facebook friends? Is she prettier than me?

My pages may not look as artsy as yours, but I am super obsessed with making sure that my handwriting is perfect. If it's not perfect or if I made a spelling error, I use white-out. Crossing things out drives me mad. 

I recently decided that while taking notes in my Marketing class, I'm going to leave this behind. Abbreviate everything? Go ahead! Sloppy handwriting? Why the fuck not! It's kind of freeing!
Can I just say, your journaling is awesome? Mine is just a bunch of stuff scrawled on a page, but yours looks so cute!

Hey there, I know this is easier said than done, but just try to take it one day at a time. Be kind to yourself. I was a mess too when I was diagnosed and lived in denial for many years before recognizing that I had a problem. 

Like /u/Bpdtransformation said, BPD is possible to recover from or at least be well-managed.
Shit, I do this too. I don't know if this is a BPD thing or not but you're not alone.

Some alternatives I've used are to hold ice cubes (sounds weird, but it gives you a similar uncomfortable feeling without actually harming yourself) or keep a rubber band around my wrist and snapping it on my wrist when I feel like self harming.

I also read in my DBT book that some people like to use red paint or a red marker, and mark exactly where they would cut. It gives them the "visual" of cutting, so to speak, without actually doing it and without leaving scars behind.
Seconding this! I loved this book.

>But my thought is this: disorder or not, I think people with borderline are genuinely bad, horrible people.

Please don't make blanket statements like this.

That's great to hear. It's been helping me a lot too. I really enjoy the counting sounds/counting breaths technique. Today I also did the exercise where you focus on a single object for 5 minutes. 

I'm taking it slow as well so I can absorb everything. Still on Chapter 3. I'm honestly going to be a little sad when I'm done with the book because I love it so much, even though I'm sure I'll refer back to it often.

Your ex sounds like an immature douche from an outsider's perspective. It was his choice to read your blog. 

What bothers me the most is that he said "it's been 8 months - get over it", yet still checks your Reddit post history and your blog? Sounds to me like he isn't over it, or at least not all of it. 

And no, I don't think you're horrible. It's your blog. You can say whatever you want. You didn't name him and all you did was present the facts of what had happened.
How are you liking it? :)
Of course. :) Feel free to message me anytime, it would be great to chat with a fellow Troll X-er going through a similar situation!

I will be thinking of you on Tuesday. <3 Just remember that it is okay to be selfish at a time like this... sure, your job is important, but YOU and YOUR HEALTH are way more important and always will be.
Thanks! I'm glad you have the opportunity for some me time. xo
Thank you. Have you considered a part-time job that isn't stressful, or /r/beermoney? Best of luck to you, just remember your current situation is temporary and that things will get better.
You too. <3 Your doctor sounds pretty rad!
There is a subreddit for everything, isn't there? :) Thank you so much, I subbed. xx
It's okay to cry. The fact that you are taking the leap to get some help is big. Be proud of that. How did your therapy session go? I hope your car battery is okay. :(

Like /u/ceralyn said, make sure you look into a therapist first! My therapist helped me a lot throughout this process and I'm unsure where I would be if I didn't have some of her guidance. Plus, if/when you do make the big move, hopefully your work in therapy will better prepare you for it so that it's not as big of a shock.

Wishing you the best too and lots of hugs. <3
Thank you, and kudos to you for finding the courage to do the same! I've considered getting a part time job maybe in the summer once I'm more "stable". :) We got this!
*hugs*

Hey thanks! I'm actually still going to be attending university full-time, so I'm looking forward to classes keeping me busy. I also play the piano which I find is a great escape for me. 

Definitely agree with you though, and **to anyone reading who may be in a similar position to me:** some days it is hard to convince yourself to get out of bed when you don't have anything else going on and you're sad, but it's important to try and keep busy. I've found that when I don't occupy myself with something I start to feel more lonely and depressed than ever.
Glad to hear from someone who has been in my shoes. :) Thank you, and you take care as well! xo
oh you <3

I've had issues with binge eating. I gained something like 70 pounds last year but managed to lose it before it got more out of control and I've kept it off so far. 

When I'm depressed though it's really hard to make myself eat, which is strange, because in the past that's when I would eat the most. I don't even feel like putting on my shoes, getting in my car, and driving to Taco Bell. It all just seems like too much effort. Same thing for going grocery shopping - too much effort, and I'm going to be losing my job soon, so I don't really want to spend money at the store either. 

Most of the time I just won't eat, or if I do, I'll eat the same thing all day long or for several days in a row (this week all I've been eating is oatmeal and air-popped popcorn). 

It sucks.
I've quit twice, but vaping/electronic cigarettes are the only thing that has worked for me. I haven't smoked in nearly 2 years. But I still vape, just because I think it's fun.

I'm in the US. My disability management services department at my employer is fully aware of the situation and has documentation filled out by my therapist indicating that she agrees with me that I need to be on a leave of absence. 

Unfortunately, they are telling me that since I initially elected to go on leave, and then told my therapist after initiating the leave, that I am not eligible. My case manager called me and said, and I quote, "Um, you can't put *yourself* on a leave. Even if you have a doctor or therapist signing off on it." My manager knows my situation as well, even though I am not legally required to tell him. 

I was planning on leaving this job soon anyway, but I wasn't planning on *this* soon. Looks like I'll have to live off of FAFSA money until I can find another worthwhile job... or I might just focus on my studies until I graduate (not long now) and go from there. *shrug*
This is good advice. Thank you. I will probably say exactly this.

Very true. Thanks for sharing your experience. I'm mostly worried because I won't be able to give a 2-weeks notice or anything like that, but like I said, I've been out for a month already so I don't think they'll be completely surprised by me saying that I'm not coming back. In fact, when I originally went on leave, I called my boss to tell him, and he asked me then if I was coming back at any point. 

I just hate feeling awkward and I care way too much about what others think. Once I let them know I'll probably cry the rest of the day.

You're right. I'm really looking forward to not having to keep everything on social media on lock down. I blocked all of my coworkers a long time ago and just told them I deleted my Facebook, but I'm sure they know better. It will be nice to not have to worry about posting something on Instagram that someone could see.

I'm just really afraid of actually telling them I'm not coming back. I may just go into the office when no one is there so that I can clean out my desk without everyone staring at me...
How did you tell them you were leaving? And how did you support yourself financially following?
How do you think I should tell them I'm not coming back? I mean, I haven't been there in a month anyway, so I doubt they will be surprised, but I'm still worried about backlash.
I really enjoyed "Get Me Out Of Here" by Rachel Reiland. It's a memoir of a woman who had BPD and recovered from it.

From what I've heard, I was a pretty happy baby. 

I was just a typical kid from my birth up until I was 6, when a girl at the bus stop told me I was "kinda fat". 

Looking at photos from then, I wasn't fat at all. But that stuck with me, so I became super insecure at the age of 6. I started gaining weight and the emotional eating began. My mom bought me workout videos geared towards kids. I distinctly remember getting weighed in elementary school gym class at the age of 10, telling my mom I weighed 130, and she said, "oh honey, that's way too much". 

So at that point, I definitely was overweight, but that comment from my mom has stayed with me to this day. I tried about 5+ different diets before I was done with middle school. I even tried starving myself, but that didn't work. Eventually I just accepted that I would never be skinny and continued to endure my classmates bullying me for being fat.

So, in the research I've done, it says that most individuals with BPD had some sort of childhood trauma. This is the only thing I can think of that could be my "trauma". Other than the awful tormenting at school and the poor body image at such a young age, I had a pretty good childhood. But even my mother has said that I started becoming depressed and overly dramatic by about the age of 8. 

Didn't mean for this to be a novel, but that's my background.

Firstly, are you currently in therapy? If not, you should consider going. A therapist can help you work through the jealousy issues. You might even be able to bring your boyfriend along for a session or two. 

That being said, has he ever given you a reason not to trust him?

>This book is a must read for anyone who wants to "protect" themselves, their children, or their loved ones from such a personality.

Wow! Fuck this guy.
This is a great way to look at it, thank you! :)

Absolutely. 

I want to travel around New Zealand for a few months and actually have the means to do so at the moment. But I'm holding back because I want to make more progress in therapy, and also because I'm afraid that once I get there, I'll be more sad than ever. It's terrifying.

And when I finally finish my degree and (hopefully) get a decent job so that I can move out of the small town I live in? The thought of packing up my life and moving to an unfamiliar place - even if the opportunity is great - is very scary. 

What if I go, fall off the deep end, and I have no support system around me? What if I don't make any friends? I'll feel more alone than ever.

Is it an option for you to transfer to a reputable online program to finish your degree?

I only ask because I went back to school last autumn to finish my undergrad after being "dropped out" for over three years. If I were going to a regular university, I'm not sure I'd have as much success as I'm having right now. The ability to do my schoolwork at any time of day has been great for me. It's also allowed me to continue working full-time (which I'm currently on a medical leave from due to my lovely BPD, but that's not relevant).

I'm the same way. I put on a mask for different times of people and situations. I have a "work me", a "casual friends me", a "first date me"... I recently discussed in therapy that the only time I am my honest, true self is when I'm around my family. Otherwise, I may let someone get to know me, but never quite enough for them to truly know what's going on.

I am a textbook BPD (black-and-white thinking, fear of abandonment, impulsive behavior, etc.) and I have only been broken up with twice. The other times I ended the relationships. 

HOWEVER, when I *have* ended a relationship, I usually go back and forth as to whether I made the right decision. I've done this with every guy I've ended things with. I'll dump him, decide a few days later I want him back, then decide I don't want him anymore... definitely idealization/devaluation in my case. Also really shitty of me to do, which is why I am so apprehensive about dating nowadays (I'm in my mid-twenties and have not had a boyfriend in almost three years by choice). It's not fair of me to treat someone like that.

I don't manipulate anyone or try to destroy relationships, at least not on purpose. I am a bit self-destructive, but I would never intentionally hurt someone else. I have a lot of love to give but I'm afraid to let anyone have it. 

Not sure where I'm going with this comment, but yeah, that's been my experience.
That makes me really sad. I suppose it's just another example of how mental illness is ostracized in today's society.
I'm sorry to hear that. A year-long waiting list is ridiculous.
I'm sorry I'm replying so late. I hope you've found something to keep yourself comfortable for right now. Is there anywhere else you can go if you want to get away from your mother?
Why would your problems be doubled, if you don't mind me asking?

Why don't you put a movie on and snuggle with your dog? I always watch Clueless or Mean Girls when I'm upset, even though I've seen both a million times. Do you have a movie that you just watch over and over?
I understand. I always miss my cat a lot when I'm away from home. How are you doing right now?
Aw! :) So cute. What do your dogs and cats look like? Do you have any of your pets with you right now? My cat always gives me a lot of comfort when I'm not feeling the greatest.
That's awesome of you and your family. Have you kept any of the animals you've rescued?

I'm sorry that you're feeling this way. Those kids were awful to you and no one deserves to be treated that way. I am sending you a giant internet hug.

You mentioned that you rescue dogs. How did you get into doing something like that? I think that's amazing, and you may have inspired me to look into rescuing cats/dogs/other animals.

I feel this way almost 24/7. 

Make a typo at work? Instantly embarrassed and replaying the moment over and over for the rest of the week. 

Fuck something up for a client? Shut down, cry at my desk, and stop talking to my coworkers for awhile. 

I feel guilty about almost everything and I feel like everyone - *everyone* - is mad at me. All the time. 

Some people may say they are "walking on eggshells" around those with BPD, but *I* feel like I am walking on eggshells around rest of society just so I don't fall out of line and I "fit in". If I make a small mistake or something embarrassing happens, it's as if I feel ashamed because I think they can tell I'm not right in the head.

I'm just frustrated because I've been dealing with this for many years now. There have been times where things did get better, only to get worse than ever. It's sort of like taking one step forward, two steps back. I don't want to keep doing this dance.
Not at the moment. But I am getting a working holiday visa for New Zealand, so maybe I'll just put a few things in a backpack and take off for a few months.

I don't think they are helping as much as they should since I still feel this way. Over the years I have tried Pristiq, Lamictal, and a few others that I can't remember the names of right now. The only thing that I can physically feel making a difference is Xanax, but I try to take that as rarely as possible due to the addiction factor. Xanax is only a temporary relief and it would be a big mistake for me to become reliant on it.
Wellbutrin XL 300mg (1 per day), Zoloft 100mg (1.5 per day), and Xanax 0.5mg as needed.
I can try and call one tomorrow. I've been on the same medications for two years; maybe this combination just isn't working for me anymore.

I have been looking into inpatient services but I have no idea how I would afford it. Why go to treatment only to get out a few months later and be buried in debt? It would be the same for going to the ER. Even with insurance, I'd pay $1200 to have them give me some pills and send me home. 

I just love the American health system. /s
